answer.rationale: Write-path p99 rose ~30 minutes after a release, during peak settlement writes. b1 is the closest analog (release rollback restored the path without a reported write-loss event) but it described an error spike, not latency, so it needs archive check. Competing load explanation (daily peak / saturation) is why b3 is verified in parallel; b3 is also a before-the-peak provisioning story, not a proven mid-peak scale-up. Circuit breaking is rejected because it sheds customer writes. Read-replica routing and regional failover lack a matching signal. Uncertainty is kept: one guarded rollback slice, not a fleet-wide cutover, until sources confirm.
